issue.description:
ADR-005's decision (2026-08-16) has no corresponding open bead, and operator documentation still describes the state in the present tense: 'bead show and bead doctor both report it as healthy' for open+assigned issues. The 583-stuck-issue fleet sweep shows the operational cost. Add a ready_frontier check under doctor's dependencies scope that warns when open issues carry an assignee, prints a bounded sample of offending ids, and states the exact remedy `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`. Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, not even under --repair (a deliberate operator reservation is indistinguishable from residue). Coordination note: doctor's dependency-scope query is separately broken — beadrs-90abfec2 (names a nonexistent column, always reports 0 blocked) — so build the new check on corrected authoritative rows, not on the broken query. Tests: assigned-open detection, bounded sample rendering, remedy string accuracy, and --repair performing no mutation.

Created by: weave strand

issue.description:
Escape hatches for the automatic default. --no-auto-flush suppresses publication for one invocation; checkpoint.auto_flush suppresses it durably for a workspace; the flag wins over configuration.

Acceptance:
- either mechanism leaves the checkpoint dirty exactly as explicit-flush behaviour does today
- sync --status reports the resulting dirty state
- the flag overrides the configuration key in both directions
- automatic publication stays silent on success, so bead create still prints only the ID plus LF

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 6-7, section 5 command table; ADR-003.
issue.notes: Implemented as 96a3a04. --no-auto-flush is a global clap arg on Cli; publication_probe disarms on it before reading .beads/config.json, so the flag wins over checkpoint.auto_flush in both directions (opted-in workspace does not publish; suppressed workspace stays suppressed). Either hatch leaves the checkpoint byte-identical and dirty (covered < live) with sync --status reporting dirty:true; sync flush-only publishes the suppressed state and leaves ready_to_commit. Two new tests in tests/post_commit_publication.rs (one-invocation suppression + override in both arg positions); item-6 silence asserted for suppressed invocations. Man pages regenerated; bead-claim.1 also picked up pre-existing --single-claim drift from beadrs-b412cc80 (that bead never regenerated). Verification: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets clean, full cargo test 42 binaries exit 0. Observation for the R026 gate (beadrs-f42b12c7): one_mutation_republishes_one_shard_and_the_event_tail in tests/checkpoint_mode_selection.rs is seed-flaky -- its bound added_bytes*16 <= corpus_bytes fails when the mutated issue's SHA-256 prefix bucket holds 2+ of the 30 issues (delta observed 1067 vs 2226 across seeds; one full-suite failure seen, not reproducible in 16 isolated runs). Pre-existing, unrelated to this change; probe script at ~/scratch/shard-flake-probe.sh.

- cargo test passes on current stable
- no forward-looking 1.75 claim remains in Cargo.toml, README.md, or AGENTS.md
